newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada cuts bank rate 25 bps to 3.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada cuts bank rate 25 bps to 3.50 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Monday cut its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.50 percent by conducting special purchase and resale operations at 3.50 percent, money market traders said.

The move lowered its target range for the overnight lending rate to 3.0-3.50 from 3.25-3.75 percent. The bank rate, at which it lends to financial institutions as lender of last resort, is the top of the central bank's target range for the overnight rate.
The bank rate, which has changed in nature over the past decades, is now at its lowest level since August 1963.

In a news release after the rate cut, the bank said recent declines in short-term market interest rates had offset the impact on monetary conditions of the movement of the Canadian dollar to a higher trading range.
The bank said that like the two previous bank rate cuts, today's action ratified this decline in market rates in order to keep monetary conditions from tightening.
Canadian T-bills firmed after the rate cut, while the currency and bonds traded steady.

The rate cut prompted several of the country's major chartered banks to lower their prime lending rates to 5.0 percent from 5.25 percent. Prime lending rates in Canada are now at their lowest level since July 1956.
It was the 10th rate cut this year by the Bank of Canada, and the 19th since the Bank of Canada began easing rates in May 1995. The central bank has now cut rates by 4.75 basis points since May 1995.
